subject: Order Form redline: assurance window, pen-test ops & evidence sprint
messages:
From: Sam Holt <sam.holt@medigen.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/Order Form redlines — clarification on assurance window and pen-test ops

Ben —

Thanks for sending the draft order form and security exhibit. Our security team had a couple of callouts in the redline (attached) that we need aligned before legal proceeds:

- Pen-test window: we prefer a 48–72 hour inspection window for scoped assessments with explicit start/end times. Can Redwood commit to a notification lead time and a point of contact for staging credentials?
- Evidence cadence: we need a bi-monthly evidence snapshot for the first 6 months post-go-live (logs, change history, SOC-2 attestations). Can you confirm retention periods for logs and a sample evidence package?
- Scoped access: we need assurance that sampled datasets will be obfuscated/pseudonymized for any live environment access.

I've attached our redline (Medigen_redline_MSASecExhibit_v1.docx). Evan (security@medigen.com) is copied to help coordinate technical logistics.

High level ask: can you route this to your legal and security leads and come back with a concrete proposal by EOD Monday (US PST)? We have procurement gating the onboarding.

Regards,
Sam Holt
Head of InfoSec, Medigen Health

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form redlines — clarification on assurance window and pen-test ops

Sam —

Appreciate the detail and the redline. Looping in our security (Karthik) and legal ops (Laura, Priyom) to propose concrete language. Quick answers while they review:

- Notification lead time: we can offer 72 hours notice for scheduled penetration tests and a 24-hour notice for expedited/critical tests (subject to mutually agreed SLA).
- Staging creds/point of contact: we will provide an access window and an escalation contact (named engineer on-call) — Karthik, can you confirm operational cadence?
- Evidence cadence & retention: Redwood retains system logs for 13 months by default; we can provide bi-monthly evidence snapshots for a 6-month ramp if consented in the order form.
- Data obfuscation: we support sampled datasets for testing; we'll need to define the obfuscation standards (hashing/pseudonymization).

I'll get back with proposed clause language from legal by Monday morning. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form redlines — clarification on assurance window and pen-test ops

Sam / Team —

Technical readout from our side:

- Pen-test window ops: we generally run tests in a designated staging slice. For production-impacting tests we require a 72-hour runway and a scoped statement of work. We can accept a 48-hour window for non-invasive vulnerability scans with a signed attestation.
- Credentials/access: we'll provision temporary, timeboxed credentials scoped to the baseline infra you list. No persistent root-level access will be provided. All activity will be logged and shared as part of the evidence bundle.
- Evidence snapshot: typical bundle includes (a) system logs (auth, API gateway, infra events) for the requested window, (b) configuration snapshots, (c) change history, and (d) SOC 2 summary report. We can redact PII from logs; pseudonymization standard should be agreed (we suggest SHA-256 hashing with per-customer salt).
- Sampling: we propose a stratified sampling plan — 3 sample days per month for the first 2 months, then monthly for months 3–6. This limits ops overhead while providing trend coverage.

Operational ask: Sam, can you confirm whether Medigen will accept redacted logs for audit purposes or whether you require full-fidelity exports? That determines our read/write procedures.

Karthik
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed language for the security exhibit & order form (redlines attached)

Sam —

Thanks for the patience. Please find proposed contract language below (high level summary; full redline attached in Drive link):

1) Penetration Tests and Inspections
- Redwood will provide at least 72 hours' notice for scheduled penetration tests conducted in production-grade environments. For non-production tests (staging), Redwood will provide 48 hours' notice.
- Redwood will provide a named operational contact and a ticket-based escalation channel during all test windows.
- Access will be timeboxed; privileged sessions will be recorded and logs exported as part of the evidence bundle.

2) Evidence & Retention
- Redwood will provide evidence snapshots on a bi-monthly cadence for the first 6 months post-go-live, then monthly for months 7–12, unless otherwise agreed. Evidence bundles will include redacted logs (auth, gateway, infra events), configuration exports, and SOC 2 attestation summary.
- Default log retention is 13 months; longer retention is available as a paid add-on and will be called out in the order form.

3) Data Handling for Tests
- Any sampled production data provided for testing will be pseudonymized by Redwood prior to exposure. Pseudonymization will use a one-way hash with a per-customer salt; re-identification keys will remain with the customer where applicable.

4) Scoped Inspection Limits
- Inspections are limited to mutually agreed components and will not include live customer content unless explicitly authorized in writing.

Next steps / asks:
- Sam: please confirm if redacted logs meet Medigen's internal audit requirements or if full-fidelity exports are required.
- Evan: propose 2 potential test windows this month for our ops team to validate resource schedules.
- Priyom: please review the attached redline and confirm any legal caveats.

If accepted, Laura will prepare an order-form addendum with the agreed cadence and a short SOW for pen-test operations.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposed language for the security exhibit & order form (redlines attached)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear draft. Quick confirmations:

- Redacted logs are acceptable for our external audit provided we can validate the sampling method and the pseudonymization approach (we'll send a short spec).
- We'll propose two windows: July 25–26 (non-invasive scans) and Aug 8–9 (scoped pen-test). Evan will drop times in the shared calendar.
- Regarding retention: 13 months is fine for now; we'll circle back if longer retention is required during procurement.

If you can produce the order-form addendum and SOW for pen-test ops by EOD Wednesday, procurement can proceed to sign-off next week.

Appreciate the collaboration.

Best,
Sam Holt
Head of InfoSec, Medigen Health
